Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

strengthen verb

also make stronger, reinforce, fortify, consolidate, build up strength, develop (character)

classical

Cic. Tusc. 2.36: corpora juvenum firmārī labōre voluērunt (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 27.13: corpora cibō (Lewis & Short)

firmō, firmāre, firmāvī, firmātum

verb, first conjugation

make firm, strengthen

Strengthen a body, a wall, a position, a resolve; to make lasting or secure.

Other words

  • cōnfirmō, cōnfirmāre, cōnfirmāvī, cōnfirmātum — strengthen, establish; reassure

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 6.21: hōc vīrēs nervōsque cōnfirmārī putant (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151

    Strengthen in body or in mind (cōnfirmā tē, take heart); also confirm, assert, and encourage. sē cōnfirmāre is to recover after an illness.

  • corrōborō, corrōborāre, corrōborāvī, corrōborātum — strengthen, invigorate

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Cael. 11: cum is jam sē corrōborāvisset (Lewis & Short)

    From rōbur: to give strength to a growing body or a virtue; sē corrōborāre is to grow up and grow strong.

Examples

  • et discās oportet et quod didicistī agendō cōnfirmēs

    you must learn, and strengthen what you have learned by doing itSen. Ep. 94.47

See also strength, improve, weak.
